Along the way also: added an HTML reporter to `playwright.config.js` (every project except `p0` had been silently producing an empty `playwright-report/` — CI failures were undebuggable from artifacts alone); fixed a webpack-build-race (`wait-on` only confirms the port is open, not that the client bundle finished compiling — added a step polling `dev-server.log` for `webpack built client`); fixed the original missing-Commerce-API-env-vars bug (job now binds `environment: dev`, sources `COMMERCE_API_*` from `vars.*`, `scripts/switchEnv.mjs`'s `push <tier>` uploads a shared+tier merge so one environment binding is self-sufficient); switched the job gate from `always()` to `!cancelled()` so a superseded/cancelled run doesn't burn a 15-min runner slot.
    86	- PR #30 (`feature/gh-qa-workflow`, merged) also: deleted the unfinished `SFCC-000_guest-checkout` placeholder (never had real Adyen payment interaction, self-described `EXAMPLE` in its own header) and its `testIgnore` mis-scoping (ran under `chromium`/`mobile-chrome` `retries:2` instead of the dedicated `p0` project's `retries:0`, costing ~12 of the ~14 min `e2e-localhost` runtime on every PR); added a homepage smoke test (new `homepage` E2E area + `SMOKE-` naming convention for Jira-less tests); fixed a `@typescript-eslint/no-var-requires` misconfiguration flagging `require()` in `e2e/`'s intentionally-CommonJS files; added `test-results/`/`playwright-report/` to `.gitignore`.
    87	- **Proposed: tag-based environment promotion (GitFlow) — full spec on Confluence, implementation not yet started.** Full rationale, tag naming convention, worked commands, and open questions:

    89	  (Confluence, v5, child of the Branching Guide page). Summary: only `Dev` should be continuously tied to `develop`; every other tier should deploy a specific, immutable git tag (`vX.Y.Z-rc.N` / `vX.Y.Z` / `vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N`, cut via `npm version`) instead of a branch ref, so Test/SIT/UAT/Stage can each run independent testing cycles instead of being forced onto the same moving branch. **Do not implement the AGENTS.md/governance pieces without squad-lead + Integration-lead sign-off — this is still a proposal.** Implementation checklist for a fresh session on a new branch (see the Confluence page for full detail on each item):
    90	  - **Decided 2026-07-16** (see Confluence page's "Decisions made so far" table): release cadence is per-sprint; pre-launch versioning starts at `v0.1.0` (MAJOR locked at `0` until go-live, which becomes `v1.0.0`); `Test` gets its own automated CI gate (not manual-only); tag protection + the version-guard + Release-per-final-tag are all adopted immediately, not phased in.

This genuinely hard-blocks a non-matching tag at push time *and* prevents force-push/delete on matching tags — all on GitHub.com, not Enterprise Server-only (corrected from an earlier draft of this note, which wrongly split this into a separate "tag protection rules" step and claimed pattern-blocking wasn't possible on GitHub.com). Keep a `push: tags: ['*']` validation workflow too, as defense-in-depth / for a clearer failure message than the raw ruleset rejection gives.
    94	    3. A version-guard step added to each `deploy-*.yml` (test/sit/stg/uat/prod) — fetch the environment's current deployed tag via `gh api repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/deployments?environment=<env>`, semver-compare against the tag being deployed (use the `semver` npm package, not hand-rolled bash comparison — pre-release identifiers must be dot-separated, e.g. `-rc.10` vs `-rc.2`, or numeric comparison breaks), fail on a downgrade. **`<env>` must be the actual GitHub Environment name, not the workflow-file suffix** — they diverge for `stg` (`deploy-stg.yml` targets the `staging` Environment, not `stg`; we hit this exact mismatch once already this session, commit `12bf91b`). 93	    2. **Primary enforcement — one GitHub Ruleset covers both naming and immutability:** Settings → Rules → Rulesets → New tag ruleset, targeting `v*`, with a "tag name pattern" rule requiring `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-rc\.\d+|-hotfix\.\d+)?$` plus "restrict creation," "restrict updates," and "restrict deletion" all enabled. This genuinely hard-blocks a non-matching tag at push time *and* prevents force-push/delete on matching tags — all on GitHub.com, not Enterprise Server-only (corrected from an earlier draft of this note, which wrongly split this into a separate "tag protection rules" step and claimed pattern-blocking wasn't possible on GitHub.com).     38	Use a compact table for the file/tier list. One short paragraph for the verdict. If rewriting, show the improved prompt in a code block.

1	---
     2	name: qa-generate
     3	description: Generate a Gherkin .feature file and Playwright test spec from a Jira story. Human-in-the-lead — Lead QA validates the .feature before Playwright is generated. Use for any new storefront user journey that needs E2E test coverage.
     4	---
     5	
     6	QA test generation is a two-step, human-gated process. Do not generate the Playwright spec
     7	until the `.feature` file has been explicitly confirmed by Lead QA.
     8	
     9	> **Three testing layers in this project** (per [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md)):
    10	> - Vitest — unit logic
    11	> - Storybook `play` functions — component interactions
    12	> - Playwright — E2E user journeys (this skill)
    13	>
    14	> The gherkin → Playwright workflow below is the **E2E layer only**. It does not replace
    15	> the Vitest / Storybook layers — write all three where each applies.
    16	
    17	> **Status:** the `e2e/` directory and Playwright harness must be in place before running this skill.
    18	> If `e2e/` does not yet exist, stop and tell the developer the QA harness must land first.
    19	
    20	---
    21	
    22	## Phase 1 — Gather story details
    23	
    24	Ask these questions one at a time. Wait for the answer before asking the next.
    25	
    26	1. What is the Jira story key? (e.g. SFCC-142)
    27	2. What is the story title?
    28	3. What are the acceptance criteria? (paste them directly)
    29	4. Which squad owns this story? (Squad A: checkout/cart/payments — Squad B: PDP/PLP/search/account)
    30	5. Which sprint is this? (Check `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` — flag if the story references a later-sprint dependency)
    31	6. Is this a P0 journey? (P0 = Digital SIT gate critical path: guest checkout, registered checkout, PDP variant selection, ATC, auth)
    32	
    33	---
    34	
    35	## Phase 2 — Draft the .feature file
    36	
    37	Write the Gherkin file to:
    38	`e2e/features/{area}/{JIRA-KEY}_{short-description}.feature`
    39	
    40	Follow the standard in `e2e/features/README.md`:
    41	- Tags: `@{JIRA-KEY} @{area}` — add `@p0` if confirmed in Phase 1
    42	- Feature block with persona, goal, and value
    43	- Background block for shared preconditions
    44	- At least one happy path scenario and one failure/edge scenario
    45	- Plain English only — no selectors, URLs, or implementation detail
    46	- Under 150 lines — split by scenario group if longer
    47	
    48	**Stop here. Do not generate the Playwright test yet.**
    49	
    50	Present the draft and say:
    51	> "This is the draft `.feature` file. Please share it with Lead QA for validation.
    52	> When QA has approved or annotated it, reply with their feedback and I will proceed."
    53	
    54	---
    55	
    56	## Phase 3 — Apply QA annotations (if any)
    57	
    58	If Lead QA returns annotations in this format:
    59	```
    60	# QA ANNOTATION: [correction]
    61	```
    62	
    63	Update the `.feature` file to reflect the correction. Confirm the change explicitly:
    64	> "Updated [what changed]. No other changes made."
    65	
    66	Repeat until Lead QA confirms the file is correct.
    67	
    68	---
    69	
    70	## Phase 4 — Generate the Playwright spec
    71	
    72	Only proceed when Lead QA has confirmed the `.feature` file.
    73	
    74	Write the Playwright test to:
    75	- `e2e/tests/zimm/{area}/{JIRA-KEY}_{description}.spec.ts` — for standard tests
    76	- `e2e/tests/zimm/{area}/{JIRA-KEY}_{description}.p0.spec.ts` — for P0 tests
    77	
    78	Rules:
    79	- Files are TypeScript (`.spec.ts`) — the TS-only convention applies to E2E too.
    80	- Import Page Objects from `e2e/support/pages/` — never use raw selectors in the test file.
    81	- Selector priority in POMs: accessible selectors (role + accessible name, label, text) > semantic HTML attributes (alt, title) > `data-testid` (only when no semantics apply). See [.claude/rules/testing.md](../../rules/testing.md).
    82	- Import fixtures from `e2e/fixtures/` — never hardcode test data. Fixtures must be keyed by `SITE_ID` (Zimmermann has 8 storefronts across 11 active locales).
    83	- Test description must match the Scenario name in the `.feature` file exactly.
    84	- Use `waitForSelector` or `waitForResponse` — never `waitForTimeout`.
    85	- Under 200 lines — extract shared logic to `e2e/support/helpers/` if needed.
    86	- **Every `test()` call must carry two Playwright tags: the `.feature` file's `@area` tag AND
    87	  its `@{JIRA-KEY}` tag** from Phase 2, e.g. `test('...', {tag: ['@checkout', '@SFCC-142']},
    88	  async ({page}) => {...})`. The `@area` tag is what `develop`-targeted PRs use to run only the
    89	  specs relevant to a diff — see [.claude/rules/testing.md > Change-scoped
    90	  E2E](../../rules/testing.md#change-scoped-e2e-develop-targeted-prs-only). The `@{JIRA-KEY}`
    91	  tag is what lets `e2e-browserstack` scope a Zephyr-linked BrowserStack run to just this
    92	  story when its key is referenced on a PR — see [.claude/rules/testing.md > BrowserStack story
    93	  scoping](../../rules/testing.md#browserstack-story-scoping). A missing or mismatched `@area`
    94	  tag doesn't lose coverage (the full-suite fallback still catches it) but a missing
    95	  `@{JIRA-KEY}` tag means BrowserStack has nothing to run for this story at all — get both right.
    96	- **If `{area}` doesn't already have an allow-list group in `.github/workflows/qa.yml`'s
    97	  `detect-changes` job** (check the `Get changed files` step — `e2e_checkout` exists today),
    98	  flag this to the developer: a new area needs its own allow-list group added there before
    99	  scoping will work for it. Propose the group (the paths this spec's Page Objects and the
   100	  component/page folders it exercises live under) rather than adding it yourself, since it's a
   101	  Tier 1 CI/CD file — see [.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md](../../rules/frozenFiles.md).
   102	
   103	---
   104	
   105	## Phase 5 — Check for new Page Object needs

1	# Gherkin Feature Files
     2	
     3	Source of truth for all Zimmermann test scenarios. Lead QA validates these files. Playwright
     4	specs are generated from them — never the other way around.
     5	
     6	---
     7	
     8	## File naming
     9	
    10	```
    11	{JIRA-KEY}_{short-description}.feature
    12	```
    13	
    14	Example: `SFCC-142_guest-checkout.feature`
    15	
    16	---
    17	
    18	## Required tags
    19	
    20	Every feature file must have all three:
    21	
    22	```gherkin
    23	@SFCC-142 @checkout @p0
    24	Feature: Guest Checkout
    25	```
    26	
    27	| Tag | Purpose | Values |
    28	|---|---|---|
    29	| `@SFCC-NNN` | Jira traceability — links BrowserStack results to the story in Zephyr | Jira ticket number |
    30	| `@area` | Functional area | `homepage`, `checkout`, `search`, `account`, `pdp`, `plp`, `integrations` |
    31	| `@p0` | Critical path — feeds the Digital SIT gate | Only on highest-risk journeys |
    32	
    33	P0 journeys (the Digital SIT gate runs these on every release PR):
    34	- Guest checkout completion
    35	- Registered checkout completion
    36	- PDP load and variant selection
    37	- Add to cart and remove from cart
    38	- Account login and logout
    39	
    40	---
    41	
    42	## Format
    43	
    44	```gherkin
    45	@SFCC-NNN @area @p0
    46	Feature: [Feature name matching Jira story title]
    47	  As a [persona]
    48	  I want to [goal]
    49	  So that [value]
    50	
    51	  Background:
    52	    Given I am on the Zimmermann storefront
    53	    And [any shared precondition]
    54	
    55	  Scenario: [Happy path — descriptive name]
    56	    Given [precondition]
    57	    When [action]
    58	    Then [expected outcome]
    59	
    60	  Scenario: [Failure or edge case]
    61	    Given [precondition]
    62	    When [action]
    63	    Then [expected outcome]
    64	```
    65	
    66	Rules:
    67	- One `.feature` file per Jira story — split by scenario group if over 150 lines
    68	- At least one happy path and one failure/edge scenario per file
    69	- `Background` block for shared preconditions — never repeat setup in each scenario
    70	- Plain English only — no selectors, no technical detail, no code references
    71	- When Lead QA annotates a correction, update the `.feature` file first, then run `/qa-generate`
    72	
    73	---
    74	
    75	## Smoke tests (no Jira story)
    76	
    77	A smoke test is exempt from the whole **Rules** list above, not just the Jira-key naming/tag —
    78	there's no story to split by scenario group, and a basic "does this page load at all" check
    79	doesn't need a documented failure/edge scenario. For a basic infrastructure/sanity check that
    80	isn't tied to a Jira story, skip the `{JIRA-KEY}_` filename prefix and the `@SFCC-NNN` tag —
    81	same reasoning as the Magento baseline files below: nothing to attribute BrowserStack/Zephyr
    82	results to.
    83	
    84	Naming: `SMOKE-{area}-{behaviour}.feature`
    85	
    86	Tags: `@{area} @smoke` only — no `@p0` (smoke tests don't gate a release) and no Jira key tag.
    87	
    88	## Magento baseline regression
    89	
    90	Files in `features/regression/` document expected Magento 2 behaviour for parity validation.
    91	
    92	Naming: `BASELINE-{area}-{behaviour}.feature`
    93	
    94	When a baseline test fails against SFCC:
    95	1. Do NOT update the test to pass
    96	2. Add a comment: `# DELTA: SFCC behaviour differs — [description]`
    97	3. Surface to Lead QA — they decide: bug, intentional change, or SFCC platform constraint
    98	
    99	---
   100	
   101	## Generating the Playwright test
   102	
   103	Once Lead QA has validated a `.feature` file, run `/qa-generate` in a Claude Code session.
   104	The skill reads the validated file and produces:
   105	- `e2e/tests/zimm/{area}/{JIRA-KEY}_{description}.spec.ts` (or `.p0.spec.ts` if tagged `@p0`)
   106	- Any new Page Object additions needed
   107	
   108	## CI gates
   109	
   110	| Trigger | What runs | Environment |
   111	|---|---|---|
   112	| PR → `develop` | Change-scoped — only the `@area` tag(s) touched by the diff (falls back to the full suite for a shared/global-impact path, or any path no area has claimed) — desktop Chromium + mobile Chrome | `npm start` on localhost, SFCC dev API |
   113	| PR → `develop`, Jira key referenced | BrowserStack, scoped to that story's `@SFCC-NNN` tag(s) only. No key referenced in the PR title/body/branch → BrowserStack doesn't run at all | SFCC SIT environment |
   114	| PR → `release/**` | Full suite, unscoped — desktop Chromium + mobile Chrome | `npm start` on localhost, SFCC dev API |
   115	| PR → `release/**` | Full suite on BrowserStack (Chrome, Safari, Firefox), unscoped — a release aggregates a whole sprint's stories, so per-story scoping doesn't apply here | SFCC SIT environment |
   116	| Push/PR on `release/**` | P0 suite only (`*.p0.spec.ts`) via Digital SIT gate | SFCC SIT environment |
   117	
   118	Change-scoping mechanics (which paths map to which `@area`, and the exact narrowing rule) live
   119	in `.github/workflows/qa.yml`'s `detect-changes` job — see
   120	[.claude/rules/testing.md > Change-scoped E2E](../../.claude/rules/testing.md#change-scoped-e2e-develop-targeted-prs-only).
   121	Every spec's Playwright tag must match its `.feature` file's `@area` tag above, or it only ever
   122	runs via the full-suite fallback.
   123	
   124	BrowserStack story-scoping mechanics (Jira key detection, `--grep` scoping, the release-always-
   125	full-suite exception) live in
   126	[.claude/rules/testing.md > BrowserStack story scoping](../../.claude/rules/testing.md#browserstack-story-scoping).
   127	A spec needs its `@SFCC-NNN` tag alongside its `@area` tag for BrowserStack scoping to find it.
   128	
   129	A PR cannot merge to `develop` until all three QA jobs pass: Vitest, Storybook, and Playwright.

1	---
     2	name: feature-spec
     3	description: Turn a plain-English feature request into a scoped implementation plan before any code is written. Asks one clarifying question at a time, then produces a spec Claude Code can execute safely. Use this before starting any non-trivial implementation session.
     4	---
     5	
     6	Produce a scoped implementation spec for a feature before any code is written.
     7	Follow each phase in order. Do not write code — this skill produces a plan only.
     8	
     9	---
    10	
    11	## Phase 1 — Clarification (one question at a time)
    12	
    13	Read the feature description the user has provided.
    14	
    15	Identify what is unclear or under-specified. Then ask ONE clarifying question — the most
    16	important one. Wait for the answer. Ask the next question only after receiving a response.
    17	
    18	Continue until you have answers to all of these (stop earlier if the feature is simple):
    19	
    20	- Which sprint does this belong to? (reference `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` when present)
    21	- Which PRD in [.docs/prd/](../../../.docs/prd/) is the source of truth for this feature? Cite section + requirement ID.
    22	- Is this Zimmermann-specific or an enhancement to an existing PWA Kit pattern?
    23	- Which squad owns the primary files involved? (A: checkout/cart/payments — B: PDP/PLP/search/account)
    24	- Are there any Tier 1 or Tier 2 files that will need to change?
    25	- Does this touch any third-party integration (Global-e, Adyen, Contentful, Searchspring/Einstein, Didomi, Omneo, Emarsys, AP21, Narvar, Google Maps)?
    26	- What does "done" look like — what is the acceptance criterion?
    27	- Are there any consent / Didomi gating requirements for scripts the feature loads?
    28	
    29	Do not ask about things the feature description already makes clear.
    30	
    31	---
    32	
    33	## Phase 2 — Parallel research
    34	
    35	Once clarification is complete, spawn three agents in parallel to research the codebase.
    36	Each agent is independent and self-contained.
    37	
    38	**Agent A — Registry / file scan:**
    39	_If `.claude/registry/` exists_, read `.claude/registry/components.md`,
    40	`hooks.md`, and `utils.md`. _Otherwise_, do a direct scan: `find overrides/app/components overrides/app/hooks overrides/app/utils -type f` and grep for anything relevant.
    41	Return: a list of relevant existing assets with their file paths.
    42	
    43	**Agent B — Pattern scan:**
    44	Find the most similar existing feature in the codebase under `overrides/app/`.
    45	Look for a component or page that has a similar interaction pattern or data shape.
    46	Read its implementation to understand the conventions used (how it calls hooks, how it
    47	handles loading/error states, how it structures its JSX, which Chakra components it uses).
    48	Return: the path of the most similar existing implementation and a brief description of
    49	the pattern it uses.
    50	
    51	**Agent C — Upstream check:**
    52	Search `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/` for any existing upstream implementation
    53	of this feature or a related one. If found, assess whether the copy-first override workflow
    54	(see [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) — "Copy-first rule") should be applied.
    55	Return: upstream file path if found, and a Take / Override / Skip recommendation.
    56	
    57	Wait for all three agents to return before proceeding to Phase 3.
    58	
    59	---
    60	
    61	## Phase 3 — Sprint check
    62	
    63	Reference `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` (when present) and [.docs/memory/projectState.md](../../../.docs/memory/projectState.md).
    64	
    65	State which sprint this feature belongs to and confirm all its dependencies exist.

1	---
     2	name: generate-changelog
     3	description: Generate a release changelog from conventional commits and upstream baseline notes. Produces audience-specific outputs for the dev team, QA, product, and GitHub Release. Use before cutting a release branch or when preparing release notes.
     4	---
     5	
     6	Generate a structured release changelog. Ask clarifying questions one at a time,
     7	then research in parallel, then produce the output. Do not write code.
     8	
     9	---
    10	
    11	## Phase 1 — Establish the release range
    12	
    13	Ask these questions one at a time if not already provided:
    14	
    15	1. What is the release version? (e.g. `v1.2.0`)
    16	2. What is the base ref to compare from? (default: run `git describe --tags --abbrev=0` to find the last tag. If no tags exist yet, use the first commit.)
    17	3. Is there anything specific that should be highlighted or excluded from the changelog?
    18	
    19	---
    20	
    21	## Phase 2 — Parallel research
    22	
    23	Spawn three agents simultaneously. Each is self-contained.
    24	
    25	**Agent A — Git log analysis**
    26	Run: `git log [BASE_REF]..HEAD --pretty=format:"%h %s" --no-merges`
    27	Parse each commit by conventional type:
    28	- `feat` → Features
    29	- `fix` → Bug fixes
    30	- `perf` → Performance
    31	- `refactor` → Refactors (include in technical changelog only)
    32	- `test` → Test coverage (include in technical changelog only)
    33	- `docs` → Documentation (include in technical changelog only)
    34	- `build` / `ci` → Infrastructure (include in technical changelog only)
    35	- `chore` → Maintenance (omit from product/QA changelogs unless `chore(deps)`)
    36	- `upstream-sync` → Upstream sync (separate section)
    37	- `style` → Omit from all changelogs
    38	
    39	For each `feat` and `fix`, extract the scope (if present) and description.
    40	Group commits under their type. Return the full categorised list.
    41	
    42	**Agent B — Upstream baseline scan**
    43	Read [.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md](../../../.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md).
    44	Identify whether the `@salesforce/retail-react-app` version changed between BASE_REF and HEAD.
    45	Use `git log [BASE_REF]..HEAD -- .docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md package.json` to find any bump.
    46	Return: the version bump (if any) and a one-sentence summary.
    47	
    48	**Agent C — New components / hooks scan**
    49	If `.claude/registry/` exists, run:
    50	`git diff [BASE_REF]..HEAD -- .claude/registry/`
    51	and parse for new entries in `components.md`, `hooks.md`, `utils.md`, `pages.md`.
    52	Otherwise, fall back to:
    53	`git log [BASE_REF]..HEAD --diff-filter=A --name-only -- 'overrides/app/components/**' 'overrides/app/hooks/**' 'overrides/app/pages/**' 'overrides/app/utils/**'`
    54	Return: lists of new components, hooks, utils, and pages added in this release.
    55	
    56	Wait for all three agents before proceeding.
    57	
    58	---
    59	
    60	## Phase 3 — Sprint context
    61	
    62	Read `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` and [.docs/memory/projectState.md](../../../.docs/memory/projectState.md). Identify which sprint(s) were completed or progressed
    63	in this release cycle. State it in one sentence for the product changelog.
    64	
    65	---
    66	
    67	## Phase 4 — Generate the changelog
    68	
    69	Produce the following four sections. Write them into a single file at:
    70	`docs/releases/[TODAY]-[VERSION].md` (create the directory if it doesn't exist).
    71	
    72	---
    73	
    74	```markdown
    75	# Release [VERSION] — [TODAY]
    76	
    77	---
    78	
    79	## 🛠 Technical Changelog (Dev Team)
    80	
    81	### New components & hooks
    82	[From Agent C — list each new component and hook with its path under overrides/app/]
    83	
    84	### Features
    85	[From Agent A feat commits — scope: description]
    86	
    87	### Bug fixes
    88	[From Agent A fix commits — scope: description]
    89	
    90	### Performance
    91	[From Agent A perf commits]
    92	
    93	### Upstream sync
    94	[From Agent B — `@salesforce/retail-react-app` version bump (if any), what was reviewed]
    95	
    96	### Refactors & test coverage
    97	[From Agent A refactor and test commits]
    98	
    99	### Dependencies & infrastructure
   100	[From Agent A build, ci, chore(deps) commits]
   101	
   102	---
   103	
   104	## 🧪 QA Changelog (Test Team)
   105	
   106	### What changed that needs testing
   107	[For each feat and fix commit, one bullet: what changed and which user journey to test.
   108	Reference the relevant P0 test if one covers it. Flag any area where a P0 test does NOT exist.]
   109	
   110	### High-risk areas this release
   111	[Any changes to: checkout flow, auth, pricing, cart, product display, navigation, consent (Didomi), international (Global-e).
   112	State what specifically changed and the blast radius.]
   113	
   114	### Regression watch
   115	[Any changes to shared components (Tier 2) or shared hooks. List the component and
   116	all known consumers that should be spot-checked.]
   117	
   118	---
   119	
   120	## 📣 Product Changelog (Business / Stakeholders)
   121	
   122	### Sprint progress
   123	[From Phase 3 — one sentence on sprint completion]
   124	
   125	### What's new
   126	[feat commits only, in plain English, no technical detail. Group by user-facing feature area.]
   127	
   128	### What's fixed
   129	[fix commits only, in plain English. Focus on customer-facing fixes only.]
   130	
   131	### What's coming next
   132	[One sentence on the next sprint focus from .docs/memory/sprintScope.md]
   133	
   134	---
   135	
   136	## 🚀 GitHub Release Summary
   137	
   138	**[VERSION]** — [TODAY]
   139	
   140	[2–3 sentence summary suitable for the GitHub Release page. Highlights the biggest
   141	feature additions and most significant fixes. Suitable for external visibility.]
   142	
   143	**Full changelog:** `docs/releases/[TODAY]-[VERSION].md`
   144	**Release notes reviewed by:** [FILL IN]
   145	```
   146	
   147	---
   148	
   149	## Phase 5 — Offer GitHub Release draft
   150	
   151	After writing the file, ask:
   152	> "Would you like me to create a GitHub Release draft using this summary?
   153	> Run: `gh release create [VERSION] --draft --title '[VERSION]' --notes '[SUMMARY]'`"
   154	
   155	Do not run the command — provide it for the developer to execute.
   156	
   157	---
   158	
   159	## Notes
   160	
   161	- If commits mix conventional and non-conventional format (transition period), flag
   162	  the non-conventional commits separately as "Uncategorised" and note they couldn't
   163	  be automatically classified.
   164	- If the base ref does not exist (first release), use `--all` for the git log.
   165	- Always omit commit hashes from the product and QA sections — they are technical noise.

     2	name: project-init
     3	description: One-time project setup walkthrough. Runs the state detection script, fixes automatable items, asks one question at a time for human-input items, and updates the 7.1c CI/CD & Environment Setup Checklist Confluence page as each item is confirmed. Run this once when setting up the project for the first time, or when returning to check setup status.
     4	---
     5	
     6	This skill has five phases. Do not skip ahead — the script output in Phase 1 determines
     7	which phases are needed and in what order.
     8	
     9	---
    10	
    11	## Phase 1 — Run the state detector
    12	
    13	Run the check script:
    14	```bash
    15	bash scripts/projectInitCheck.sh
    16	```
    17

1	# Skills — What They Are and How to Use Them
     2	
     3	This is the canonical reference for every skill in this folder. If you're looking for _why_
     4	the skill system exists (the human-in-the-lead design philosophy), see the
     5	[Human-in-the-Lead AI Development — Project Setup Overview](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/305102849)
     6	Confluence page (Part 2: AI Governance Layer) —
     7	that page covers the rationale; this file covers the _mechanics_: what each skill does, what
     8	to pass it, and what it hands back.
     9	
    10	## How skills work
    11	
    12	- Invoke a skill by typing `/skill-name` (optionally followed by an argument) in a Claude
    13	  Code session. Each skill is a structured, reviewable process defined in its own
    14	  `<skill-name>/SKILL.md` file — not a freeform prompt.
    15	- Where a skill takes an argument, its `SKILL.md` uses `$ARGUMENTS` to capture whatever
    16	  follows the skill name, e.g. `/new-component productBadge` or `/audit-tier overrides/app/hooks/use-wish-list.ts`.
    17	  If you invoke a skill with no argument and one is expected, Claude asks for it.
    18	- Every skill is **human-in-the-lead**: it either stops for confirmation at a defined
    19	  checkpoint, or produces a read-only report/plan rather than making changes outright.
    20	  See the checkpoint column in each table below.
    21	- These `SKILL.md` files are also the master source for `.cursor/rules/skills/*.mdc` and
    22	  `.vscode/instructions/workflows.md` — see [scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs](../../scripts/syncCursorRules.mjs).
    23	  Edit the `SKILL.md` here, then run `npm run sync:ai-rules:fix`; never edit the generated
    24	  Cursor/VS Code files directly.
    25	
    26	## Setup & onboarding
    27	
    28	| Skill                                      | Usage            | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Human-in-the-lead checkpoint                                      |
    29	| ------------------------------------------ | ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
    30	| [`/session-start`](session-start/SKILL.md) | `/session-start` | Confirms the current branch is safe to work on, reads `.docs/memory/` tracking docs, runs health checks, and states current project position. Run at the **start of every session**.                                                                                                                 | Waits for you to confirm direction before writing any code        |
    31	| [`/onboarding`](onboarding/SKILL.md)       | `/onboarding`    | Interactive walkthrough for a new developer or QA engineer — role and squad questions, mechanical setup checks (git hooks, Node version, branch), then role-specific orientation to the rules and tools. Run on a **first session on a new machine or first day on the project**.                    | Confirms understanding at each phase before moving on             |
    32	| [`/project-init`](project-init/SKILL.md)   | `/project-init`  | One-time project setup walkthrough — runs `scripts/projectInitCheck.sh`, fixes automatable failures, then asks one question at a time for items that need a human answer (Jira prefix, BrowserStack, secrets, Zephyr product, etc.), updating the [7.1c CI/CD & Environment Setup Checklist](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/305430530) Confluence page as it goes. | Asks one question at a time, waits for the answer before the next |
    33	
    34	## Planning & safety
    35	
    36	| Skill                                    | Usage                                               | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Human-in-the-lead checkpoint                                             |
    37	| ---------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
    38	| [`/feature-spec`](feature-spec/SKILL.md) | `/feature-spec <plain-English feature description>` | Turns a feature request into a scoped implementation spec **before any code is written** — clarifies requirements one question at a time, researches the codebase in parallel, checks sprint scope, then outputs a spec with file list, tier flags, and a ready-to-paste Claude Code prompt. | Produces a plan only — you review the spec before implementation begins  |
    39	| [`/scope-check`](scope-check/SKILL.md)   | `/scope-check <a proposed Claude Code prompt>`      | Reviews a prompt _before you run it_ — classifies every file it would likely touch by protection tier, flags drift risk (refactoring upward, cross-squad reach), and verdicts it SAFE / RISKY / BLOCKED. Rewrites risky prompts into safely-scoped ones.                                     | You see the blast radius and verdict before the risky prompt is ever run |
    40	| [`/audit-tier`](audit-tier/SKILL.md)     | `/audit-tier <file or directory path>`              | Identifies the protection tier (1–4), owner, and import blast radius of a path under `overrides/`. Use before editing anything you're unsure about.                                                                                                                                          | Tells you who to notify before you touch the file                        |
    41	
    42	## Development
    43	
    44	| Skill                                      | Usage                            | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                      | Human-in-the-lead checkpoint                                    |
    45	| ------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
    46	| [`/new-component`](new-component/SKILL.md) | `/new-component <componentName>` | Scaffolds a new Zimmermann component under `overrides/app/components/` — TypeScript, Chakra-first, folder layout and props typing per `.claude/rules/conventions.md`/`components.md`/`css.md`, paired Storybook story, optional test file. | You name the component and confirm the resulting file structure |
    47	
    48	## Quality & review
    49	
    50	| Skill                                    | Usage                                                                                   | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Human-in-the-lead checkpoint                                                   |
    51	| ---------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
    52	| [`/code-quality`](code-quality/SKILL.md) | `/code-quality [file or directory]` (no argument = files changed on the current branch) | **Read-only** audit against `.claude/rules/conventions.md`, `typescript.md`, `css.md`, and `components.md` — naming/structure, circular imports, TypeScript coverage, test/story existence. Produces a prioritised 🔴/🟡/🔵 report. Use after implementing a feature or before opening a PR. | Report only — you decide what to fix and when                                  |
    53	| [`/pr-checklist`](pr-checklist/SKILL.md) | `/pr-checklist`                                                                         | Runs `/code-quality` on the current branch's changed files, classifies each by tier and reviewer requirement, and generates a copy-paste-ready PR description with a test checklist. Pairs with `/code-quality`.                             | You review and submit the generated PR description — nothing is posted for you |
    54	
    55	## QA / testing
    56	
    57	| Skill                                  | Usage                                              | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | Human-in-the-lead checkpoint                                                    |
    58	| -------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
    59	| [`/qa-generate`](qa-generate/SKILL.md) | `/qa-generate` (then answers Jira story questions) | Two-step, human-gated E2E test generation: drafts a Gherkin `.feature` file and **stops completely**; only generates the Playwright spec after Lead QA has explicitly validated (and optionally annotated) the feature file. Use for any new storefront user journey needing E2E coverage. | Playwright spec is not generated until Lead QA signs off on the `.feature` file |
    60	
    61	## Contentful
    62	
    63	| Skill                                                                      | Usage                                                                                                  | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                               | Human-in-the-lead checkpoint                                                                              |
    64	| -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
    65	| [`/contentful-register-component`](contentful-register-component/SKILL.md) | `/contentful-register-component <component file path>`                                                 | Reads an existing component's TypeScript props, generates a `*ContentfulDefinition.ts` file mapping each prop to a Contentful variable type, and wires it into the `defineComponents` registry.            | You review the generated definition (and any skipped/ambiguous props) before it's published in Contentful |
    66	| [`/contentful-drift-check`](contentful-drift-check/SKILL.md)               | `/contentful-drift-check [component or directory path]` (no argument = scan all registered components) | **Read-only** comparison of component props against their paired Contentful definitions — reports added props, removed props, and type mismatches. Use after props change, or to audit everything at once. | Report only — you resolve any drift found                                                                 |
    67	
    68	## Release management
    69	
    70	| Skill                                                    | Usage                                                                                    | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    | Human-in-the-lead checkpoint                                                                                    |
    71	| -------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
    72	| [`/generate-changelog`](generate-changelog/SKILL.md)     | `/generate-changelog` (then answers version/range questions)                             | Builds a structured, four-audience changelog (dev team, QA, product, GitHub Release) from conventional commits and the upstream baseline. Writes to `docs/releases/`. Use before cutting a release branch.                                      | You review the changelog before it's published; the GitHub Release command is proposed, never run automatically |
    73	| [`/upstream-sync-review`](upstream-sync-review/SKILL.md) | `/upstream-sync-review` (then supply a candidate `@salesforce/retail-react-app` version) | Reviews upstream release notes against `.docs/memory/upstreamBaseline.md`, maps changes to our override surface, and recommends BUMP / DEFER / WAIT — per the "read the changelog, bump opportunistically" policy in `.docs/upstreamPolicy.md`. | Recommendation only — you approve and run the actual `npm install` bump                                         |
    74	
    75	## Adding a new skill

     3	This is the canonical reference for every skill in this folder. If you're looking for _why_
     4	the skill system exists (the human-in-the-lead design philosophy), see the
     5	[Human-in-the-Lead AI Development — Project Setup Overview](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/305102849)
     6	Confluence page (Part 2: AI Governance Layer) —

     9	
    10	## How skills work
    11	
    12	- Invoke a skill by typing `/skill-name` (optionally followed by an argument) in a Claude
    13	  Code session. Each skill is a structured, reviewable process defined in its own
    14	  `<skill-name>/SKILL.md` file — not a freeform prompt.
    15	- Where a skill takes an argument, its `SKILL.md` uses `$ARGUMENTS` to capture whatever
    16	  follows the skill name, e.g. `/new-component productBadge` or `/audit-tier overrides/app/hooks/use-wish-list.ts`.
    17	  If you invoke a skill with no argument and one is expected, Claude asks for it.

Without this contract the storefront cannot implement the call against a real MuleSoft instance. **Owner:** MuleSoft — GiveX supplies the underlying failure-code list; Zimmermann owns the final customer-facing message copy.
    77	2. **Per-environment MuleSoft endpoint, API token, and rate-limit thresholds.** MuleSoft to supply, per environment: MuleSoft host, balance-check endpoint path, MuleSoft API token, and the agreed per-IP / per-session rate-limit thresholds and the bot-management vendor in front of the MRT route. **Owner:** MuleSoft (host / token / thresholds); the MRT-edge WAF / bot / rate-limit config is ours.
    78	3. **Whether the balance-check route uses a CAPTCHA.** Confirm whether the MRT balance-check route should present a CAPTCHA challenge when the bot manager elevates a request — this is not yet decided. If a CAPTCHA is used, the simplest option is Google reCAPTCHA v3, reusing the site key already provisioned for register / login (no new provisioning). **Owner:** Zimmermann.
    79	
    80	## 6. Booxi
    81	
    82	Boutique appointment history is a PWA-direct read (PWA → MRT → Booxi); scope and timeline are TBC.
    83	
    84	1. **Storefront scope and timeline (CRM-165 – CRM-167).** Confirm whether the My Account appointments surface is read-only history (current assumption) or whether in-storefront booking / rescheduling / cancellation is also in scope, and confirm the target sprint. Until confirmed, the section is built read-only and structured to slot in without redesign.
    85	2. **Booxi API specification.** Booxi to publish the API contract for appointment history — endpoint(s), request and response schemas, the appointment status values and their customer-facing copy, error codes, and pagination. The PWA-side types are generated from this contract.
    86	3. **Customer-identification mechanism (PWA-direct path).** Confirm how the storefront proves customer identity to Booxi without allowing the browser to retrieve an arbitrary customer's appointments — whether a Booxi customer ID is stored on the SFCC / Omneo profile (and how it is populated), or whether MRT must look the customer up in Booxi at request time. The mechanism must prevent impersonation.
    87	4. **Per-environment Booxi credentials.** Booxi to supply, per environment: Booxi API host, API credential, and the credential rotation cadence and named owner. Note the API host is region-specific (e.g. a North America vs EU base URL), so confirm which regional host serves Zimmermann.
    88	
    89	## 7. Adyen
    90	
    91	1. **Apple Pay and Google Pay merchant IDs.** Provide the Apple Pay and Google Pay merchant IDs per domain. Needed before the wallet buttons can be switched on. **Owner:** Zimmermann.
    92	2. **Per-environment Adyen credentials.** Provide, for each environment (Dev / SIT / UAT / Stage / Prod — `Test` intentionally excluded here; it's a lightweight, on-demand pre-SIT tier expected to share Dev's sandbox credentials rather than provisioning its own. Revisit if that assumption turns out to be wrong.): client key, API key, HMAC key, merchant account ID per region, and whether it's a test or live Adyen account. Without these, checkout can't be tested against a real Adyen account.
    93	
    94	## 8. Global-e
    95	
    96	1. **Iframe embedding requirements.** Global-e to confirm and supply: (a) the `Content-Security-Policy` `frame-src` value for production and non-production Global-e checkout origins — needed to configure the storefront's security headers; and (b) the `postMessage` schema and trusted sender origin for iframe resize and order-completion signals — the PWA listener must verify `event.origin` against this value before acting. Neither can be guessed; both are needed before the iframe can be built.
    97	
    98	2. **Order fields for international orders.** Confirm what order fields the PWA will receive for a Global-e order, to decide between rendering full order detail or a "View on tracking page" fallback. Full detail needs: line items, totals in both shopper and base currency, shipping address, and fulfilment status.
    99	
   100	## 9. Google Maps
   101	
   102	1. **Google Cloud Platform (GCP) project and per-environment API keys.** Zimmermann to provision one Places API key per environment (Dev / SIT / UAT / Stage / Prod — `Test` intentionally excluded here; it's a lightweight, on-demand pre-SIT tier expected to share Dev's sandbox credentials rather than provisioning its own. Revisit if that assumption turns out to be wrong.). Without the keys the integration cannot be exercised against a real Google account.
   103	
   104	## 10. reCAPTCHA
   105	
   106	1. **Per-environment reCAPTCHA site key and secret key.** Zimmermann to provision a Google Cloud project (or use an existing one) and register reCAPTCHA v3 keys for each environment's domain. Supply `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY` (public) and `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` (server-only, for MRT token verification) per environment (Dev / SIT / UAT / Stage / Prod — `Test` intentionally excluded here; it's a lightweight, on-demand pre-SIT tier expected to share Dev's sandbox credentials rather than provisioning its own. Revisit if that assumption turns out to be wrong.). Without these, bot protection cannot be exercised against a real Google account.
   107	
   108	2. **Didomi consent category and vendor / feature ID (EU and UK storefronts only).** reCAPTCHA is consent-gated in EU and UK. Zimmermann Privacy to confirm which Didomi consent category covers reCAPTCHA (no obvious prior — the purpose is bot protection, not analytics or marketing). Tell No Lies to then provide the corresponding Didomi vendor or feature ID so the consent-gated script loader can be wired correctly. **Owner:** Zimmermann Privacy / Tell No Lies.
   109	
   110	## 11. Narvar
   111	
   112	1. **Per-environment Narvar retailer ID and CONVERT API key.** Provide one set per environment (Dev / SIT / UAT / Stage / Prod — `Test` intentionally excluded here; it's a lightweight, on-demand pre-SIT tier expected to share Dev's sandbox credentials rather than provisioning its own. Revisit if that assumption turns out to be wrong.). Without these, the widget cannot be exercised against a real Narvar account.
   113	
   114	2. **Didomi consent category for Narvar Promise.** Confirm which Didomi category the CONVERT widget falls under (Performance?). This determines whether the widget loads for EU and UK users who accept Performance cookies but decline Analytics or Marketing.
   115	
   116	## 12. Didomi
   117	
   118	1. **Didomi purpose / vendor IDs.** Provide the Didomi purpose IDs backing the storefront's consent categories (Performance, Analytics, Marketing — REG-051). Also provide Didomi vendor IDs if applicable.
   119	2. **Notice IDs per environment.** Zimmermann to provision the Didomi Notices per environment (Dev / SIT / UAT / Stage / Prod — `Test` intentionally excluded here; it's a lightweight, on-demand pre-SIT tier expected to share Dev's sandbox credentials rather than provisioning its own. Revisit if that assumption turns out to be wrong.) and supply the Notice IDs so they can be wired into the per-environment configuration. Without these IDs, the SDK cannot be exercised end-to-end against a real Didomi configuration.
   120	
   121	## 13. GTM (with Tell No Lies/Zimm)
   122	
   123	1. **Addingwell tagging-server URL (per environment).** The production first-party subdomain is confirmed as `ruffles.zimmermann.com` (2026-06-09). Zimmermann/Accenture to provision the equivalent first-party host for each non-production environment (each must be first-party to that environment's storefront domain). The PWA points the loader at this URL.
   124	2. **Data layer schema confirmation.** The data layer is a single shared artifact. Tell No Lies to confirm the storefront's proposed event and attribute schema (page views, product impressions, add-to-cart, begin-checkout, purchase and related ecommerce events, plus consent state and user identifiers) satisfies both GTM's own tags (GA4, Meta) and the frontend-direct data-layer consumers (Optimizely, Crazy Egg — not GTM tags). Any additional attributes Optimizely needs for segmentation (AAB-004) or Crazy Egg needs for filtering (AAB-005) must be raised at this point.
   125	
   126	## 14. Inside Chat
   127	
   128	1. **The script tag.** From Zimmermann / Inside Chat / Tryzens (the equivalent of what Tryzens hardcoded in Magento).
   129	2. **Didomi consent category and vendor / feature ID.** Inside Chat is now a direct PWA head tag (not via GTM — confirmed 2026-07-10). Zimmermann to provide the Didomi vendor or feature ID so the consent-gated loader can be wired. **Owner:** Zimmermann Privacy / Tell No Lies.
   130	
   131	## 15. Optimizely (with Zimm/TNL)
   132	
   133	Optimizely Web is a frontend-direct script (not in GTM), gated on Didomi consent.
   134	
   135	1. **Didomi consent category and vendor / feature ID.** Zimmermann Privacy to confirm which Didomi consent category covers Optimizely (expected: Analytics). Tell No Lies to then provide the corresponding Didomi vendor or feature ID so the consent-gated loader can be wired correctly.
   136	
   137	## 16. Crazy Egg (with Zimm/TNL)
   138	
   139	Crazy Egg (heatmaps / session recording) is a frontend-direct script (not in GTM), gated on Didomi consent (category TBC — Zimmermann Privacy to confirm).
   140	
   141	1. **Crazy Egg account / site ID per environment.** Zimmermann to provide the account / site ID (script), confirming whether a single account serves all environments or one per tier.
   142	2. **Masking configuration ownership.** Confirm that Tell No Lies owns and applies the session-recording masking configuration (payment and PII fields suppressed) inside the Crazy Egg application. The storefront-side scope is confirmed (AAB-005): the PWA populates the data layer and renders maskable fields with stable selectors; masking itself is outside the PWA.
   143	3. **Didomi consent category and vendor / feature ID.** Zimmermann Privacy to confirm which Didomi consent category covers Crazy Egg (expected: Analytics). Tell No Lies to then provide the corresponding Didomi vendor or feature ID so the consent-gated loader can be wired correctly.
   144	
   145	## 17. Measmerize
   146	
   147	1. **Consent approach.** Zimmermann privacy / legal to confirm which of two approaches applies: (a) load the script freely and call `window.measmerize.tracking.disableAnalytics()` / `disableCustom()` / `cookies.disableFunctional()` when consent is denied (Essential cookies always run), or (b) gate the entire script load behind a Didomi consent category. This is a **blocking** decision. If approach (b) is chosen, Zimmermann Privacy to also confirm the Didomi consent category and Tell No Lies to supply the corresponding Didomi vendor / feature ID. **Owner:** Zimmermann.
   148	
   149	## 18. Vimeo
   150	
   151	Vimeo is used for product video (PDP) and editorial video (content pages via Contentful CMS). The embed loads client-side as a facade-loaded iframe.
   152	
   153	1. **Consent approach.** Zimmermann privacy / legal to confirm: (a) always append `dnt=1` to the embed URL — suppresses Vimeo's tracking cookies, no Didomi gate needed; or (b) load the standard embed gated behind a Didomi consent category. This is a **blocking** decision. If approach (b) is chosen, Tell No Lies to supply the Didomi vendor / feature ID. **Owner:** Zimmermann.
   154	
   155	2. **Vimeo platform confirmation (PRD-067).** The Third Party Integrations sheet lists Vimeo as the video platform, but PRD-067 is explicitly open: "Vimeo has not been 100% confirmed — open action to confirm best solution for smoothest FE experience." Zimmermann to confirm before PDP video implementation begins. **Owner:** Zimmermann.

1	---
     2	name: onboarding
     3	description: Interactive onboarding for new developers and QA engineers joining the Zimmermann PWA Kit project. Asks role at the start, checks the mechanical setup items, then orients the person to the rules and tools relevant to their role and squad. Run this in the first Claude Code session on a new machine or a first day on the project.
     4	---
     5	
     6	Welcome the developer or QA engineer and explain what this skill does in one sentence.
     7	Then proceed through the phases below. Ask one question at a time. Do not front-load.
     8	
     9	---
    10	
    11	## Phase 1 — Role and context
    12	
    13	Ask:
    14	> "Are you joining as a developer or a QA engineer?"
    15	
    16	Wait for the answer. Then:
    17	
    18	**If developer:** Ask:
    19	> "Which squad are you on — Squad A (checkout, cart, payments, order management, tax, GivX) or Squad B (Homepage, PDP, PLP, search, account, Brochureware Content)?"
    20	
    21	**If QA:** No squad question needed — QA covers both squads.
    22	
    23	Ask (both roles):
    24	> "Is this your first time working on this project, or are you returning on a new machine?"
    25	
    26	New = full walkthrough. Returning on new machine = focus on mechanical setup, skip orientation.
    27	
    28	---
    29	
    30	## Phase 2 — Mechanical setup checks
    31	
    32	Run these checks inline using the Bash tool. Report results as you go.
    33	
    34	```bash
    35	node --version
    36	npm --version
    37	claude --version 2>/dev/null || echo "NOT FOUND"
    38	command -v coderabbit &>/dev/null && { coderabbit --version; coderabbit auth status; } || echo "NOT FOUND (required)"
    39	git branch --show-current
    40	ls -la .git/hooks/ | grep -E 'pre-commit|commit-msg' || echo "hooks missing"
    41	[ -f .env.shared ] || echo ".env.shared missing"
    42	for t in dev test sit uat staging prod; do
    43	  [ -f ".env.$t" ] || echo ".env.$t missing"
    44	done
    45	[ -f .env ] || echo ".env missing"
    46	```
    47	
    48	For each issue found:
    49	
    50	**Hooks missing:**
    51	> "The git hooks aren't installed on this machine. Run both of these now:"
    52	```bash
    53	cp scripts/hooks/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit
    54	cp scripts/hooks/commit-msg .git/hooks/commit-msg && chmod +x .git/hooks/commit-msg
    55	```
    56	Verify after: `ls -la .git/hooks/ | grep -E 'pre-commit|commit-msg'`
    57	
    58	**On develop or main:**
    59	> "You're on the `{branch}` branch. You must always work on a feature branch. Create one now:"
    60	```bash
    61	git checkout -b feature/your-ticket-onboarding-setup
    62	```
    63	
    64	**Not fully initialized yet** (`.env.shared` missing, or any `.env.<tier>` file missing):
    65	> "Environment config isn't fully set up on this machine yet. Run:"
    66	```bash
    67	npm run env -- init
    68	```
    69	> "This scaffolds `.env.shared` (values shared across every tier) and one `.env.<tier>` file per
    70	> deployment tier (dev/test/sit/uat/staging/prod), pulls in whatever's already been published to
    71	> this repo's GitHub Environments (Settings > Environments), and auto-fetches your Contentful
    72	> Delivery/Preview tokens once you've filled in a personal `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN`.
    73	> Fill in any values it reports as still blank — `npm run env -- validate` shows what's missing —
    74	> then activate a tier with `npm run env -- dev` (or whichever tier you're working against).
    75	> Full command reference is in `.env.sample`'s header comment."
    76	> `init` skips any file that already exists and only scaffolds what's missing, so it's always
    77	> safe to rerun on a partially-initialized machine.
    78	
    79	**Fully initialized but no tier activated yet** (`.env.shared` and every `.env.<tier>` file present, but root `.env` missing):
    80	> "Environment config is initialized but no tier is active yet. Activate one:"
    81	```bash
    82	npm run env -- dev
    83	```
    84	> "(or whichever tier you're working against)."
    85	
    86	**Node too old:** Point to the project's node requirement (24 LTS) and ask them to update before continuing.
    87	
    88	**Claude Code not found:** `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code` then `claude login`.
    89	
    90	**CodeRabbit CLI not found or not authenticated:** Required, not optional — AGENTS.md's workflow
    91	step 4 treats a missing or unauthenticated CLI as a blocker before a non-trivial commit, not
    92	something to silently skip past. Install from https://www.coderabbit.ai/cli, then authenticate
    93	with `coderabbit auth login --api-key "$CODERABBIT_API_KEY"` — the shared key is already pulled
    94	into `.env.shared` by `npm run env -- init` (see `.env.sample`). Don't let the developer move on
    95	with this unresolved.
    96	
    97	Once all checks pass, say: "Setup is confirmed. Let's cover the rules and tools."
    98	
    99	---
   100	
   101	## Phase 3 — Developer orientation
   102	
   103	*Skip this phase for QA — go to Phase 4.*
   104	
   105	### Rules overview
   106	
   107	Walk through these in order — brief, one at a time, confirm understanding before continuing.
   108	
   109	**Branch rule (non-negotiable):**
   110	> "Never work directly on `develop` or `main`. Every task gets a feature branch.
   111	> Before each session: `git branch --show-current`. If it says develop, stop."
   112	
   113	**Protection tiers:**
   114	> "Every file in this repo has a tier. Tier 1 = frozen, you cannot touch it without explicit
   115	> owner approval. Tier 2 = protected, requires a second reviewer on the PR.
   116	> The Tier 1 list is in [.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md](../../rules/frozenFiles.md). Read it before your first task."
   117	
   118	Point them to the full tier map: [.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md](../../rules/frozenFiles.md) and [.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md](../../rules/protectedFiles.md).
   119	
   120	**TypeScript-only rule:**
   121	> "Every file you create or modify under `overrides/` must be `.ts` or `.tsx`.
   122	> `.js`/`.jsx` are not acceptable in that folder — including theme files, stories, and config modules.
   123	> Run `npx tsc --noEmit` before finishing any task that touches `overrides/`."
   124	
   125	**Hard Rule #12:**
   126	> "If requirements are unclear, Claude will ask one clarifying question at a time and wait.
   127	> If you're prompting Claude and it asks a question, answer it before sending the next instruction."
   128	
   129	**Contact map:**
   130	Read [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) contact map section. Tell them:
   131	> "Design tokens → UI Designer (#design-system). Commerce hooks → Integration Lead (#integration).
   132	> Checkout / cart → Squad A Lead. PDP / search / account → Squad B Lead."
   133	
   134	### Sprint order
   135	
   136	Read `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` and [.docs/memory/projectState.md](../../../.docs/memory/projectState.md). Tell them which sprint the project is currently in.
   137	
   138	> "We're in Sprint [N]. That means [what exists]. Code from Sprint [N+1] doesn't exist yet —
   139	> don't reference it in your tasks."
   140	
   141	### Squad-specific orientation
   142	
   143	**Squad A (checkout, cart, payments):**
   144	> "Your squad owns `overrides/app/pages/checkout/`, `overrides/app/components/order-summary/`,
   145	> `overrides/app/components/promo-code/`, and `overrides/app/components/pickup-or-delivery/`.
   146	> Before touching the header, footer, or shared product components, message Squad B Lead."
   147	
   148	**Squad B (PDP, PLP, search, account):**
   149	> "Your squad owns `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/`, `overrides/app/pages/product-list/`,
   150	> `overrides/app/pages/account/`, and `overrides/app/components/product-tile/`.
   151	> Before touching checkout or cart components, message Squad A Lead."
   152	
   153	### Key skills
   154	
   155	Tell them which skills to reach for first:
   156	- [/session-start](../session-start/SKILL.md) — run at the start of every session (mandatory)
   157	- [/feature-spec](../feature-spec/SKILL.md) — before starting any non-trivial implementation
   158	- [/code-quality](../code-quality/SKILL.md) — before opening a PR
   159	- [/pr-checklist](../pr-checklist/SKILL.md) — to generate PR description
   160	- [/qa-generate](../qa-generate/SKILL.md) — when you need E2E test coverage for a user journey
   161	
   162	### First task
   163	
   164	> "Your first task: read [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) and [.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md](../../rules/frozenFiles.md) end to end.
   165	> Then run `/session-start` to see the current project state.
   166	> When you have a ticket to work on, start with `/feature-spec` before writing any code."
   167	
   168	---
   169	
   170	## Phase 4 — QA orientation
   171	
   172	*Skip this phase for developers — they went through Phase 3.*
   173	
   174	### The QA model
   175	
   176	> "This project uses a human-in-the-lead QA model. Claude generates tests — you validate them.
   177	> A test is not complete until you have approved the Gherkin `.feature` file.
   178	> Never accept a Playwright spec without reading and confirming the `.feature` file first."
   179	
   180	### Testing layers
   181	
   182	Three layers, three purposes (per [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) > Testing):
   183	1. **Vitest** — unit logic.
   184	2. **Storybook `play` functions** — component interactions.
   185	3. **Playwright** — E2E user journeys (this is where Gherkin lives).
   186	
   187	### Feature file workflow
   188	
   189	Walk through the workflow:
   190	1. Developer creates a Jira story.
   191	2. Developer runs [/qa-generate](../qa-generate/SKILL.md) in Claude Code.
   192	3. Claude drafts a Gherkin `.feature` file and **stops**.
   193	4. QA reads the `.feature` file — it's in `e2e/features/{area}/`.
   194	5. QA annotates corrections in the file with `# QA ANNOTATION: [correction]`.
   195	6. Developer runs `/qa-generate` again with the annotation.
   196	7. Claude updates the feature file (confirm), then generates the Playwright spec.
   197	
   198	Point them to `e2e/features/README.md` and the [Guide 4: E2E Testing — Playwright & Gherkin Repo Conventions](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/305528833) Confluence page.
   199	
   200	### Tags they must verify
   201	
   202	Every `.feature` file needs:
   203	- `@{JIRA-KEY}` — Jira traceability for Zephyr. **If missing, results won't sync.**
   204	- `@{area}` — functional area tag
   205	- `@p0` — only on confirmed critical paths (checkout, ATC, auth, PDP variant selection)
   206	
   207	> "If a feature file is missing the Jira tag, flag it to the developer before the test is generated."
   208	
   209	### Magento baseline regression
   210	
   211	> "Files in `e2e/features/regression/` document Magento 2 expected behaviour.
   212	> When a baseline test fails against SFCC, do NOT update it to pass.
   213	> Add `# DELTA:` and bring it to the next standup for classification."
   214	
   215	### BrowserStack and Zephyr
   216	
   217	> "BrowserStack cross-browser runs trigger automatically on PRs to `release/**`.
   218	> Results link to your Zephyr stories via BrowserStack Test Observability.
   219	> Check with the delivery lead that your Jira account has access to the BrowserStack project."
   220	
   221	### First task
   222	
   223	> "Your first task: read the [Guide 4: E2E Testing — Playwright & Gherkin Repo Conventions](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/305528833) Confluence page end to end.
   224	> Then review the reference `.feature` file under `e2e/features/checkout/`. If you spot anything that reads like a technical implementation detail rather than plain English, that's exactly the kind of thing to flag in an annotation."
   225	
   226	---
   227	
   228	## Phase 5 — Confirm and close
   229	
   230	Ask:
   231	> "Any questions before you start?"
   232	
   233	Answer questions, one at a time. Then close with:
   234	> "You're set up. Run `/session-start` at the start of every session — it reads the tracking
   235	> docs and confirms where the project is before any code is written.
   236	> If something is unclear mid-task, ask in #dev-team before running Claude Code on it."

    56	Verify after: `ls -la .git/hooks/ | grep -E 'pre-commit|commit-msg'`
    57	
    58	**On develop or main:**
    59	> "You're on the `{branch}` branch. You must always work on a feature branch. Create one now:"
    60	```bash
    61	git checkout -b feature/your-ticket-onboarding-setup
    62	```
    63	
    64	**Not fully initialized yet** (`.env.shared` missing, or any `.env.<tier>` file missing):
    65	> "Environment config isn't fully set up on this machine yet. Run:"
    66	```bash
    67	npm run env -- init
    68	```
    69	> "This scaffolds `.env.shared` (values shared across every tier) and one `.env.<tier>` file per
    70	> deployment tier (dev/test/sit/uat/staging/prod), pulls in whatever's already been published to
    71	> this repo's GitHub Environments (Settings > Environments), and auto-fetches your Contentful
    72	> Delivery/Preview tokens once you've filled in a personal `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN`.
    73	> Fill in any values it reports as still blank — `npm run env -- validate` shows what's missing —
    74	> then activate a tier with `npm run env -- dev` (or whichever tier you're working against).
    75	> Full command reference is in `.env.sample`'s header comment."
    76	> `init` skips any file that already exists and only scaffolds what's missing, so it's always
    77	> safe to rerun on a partially-initialized machine.
    78	
    79	**Fully initialized but no tier activated yet** (`.env.shared` and every `.env.<tier>` file present, but root `.env` missing):
    80	> "Environment config is initialized but no tier is active yet. Activate one:"
    81	```bash
    82	npm run env -- dev
    83	```
    84	> "(or whichever tier you're working against)."
    85	
    86	**Node too old:** Point to the project's node requirement (24 LTS) and ask them to update before continuing.
    87	
    88	**Claude Code not found:** `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code` then `claude login`.
    89	
    90	**CodeRabbit CLI not found or not authenticated:** Required, not optional — AGENTS.md's workflow
    91	step 4 treats a missing or unauthenticated CLI as a blocker before a non-trivial commit, not
    92	something to silently skip past. Install from https://www.coderabbit.ai/cli, then authenticate
    93	with `coderabbit auth login --api-key "$CODERABBIT_API_KEY"` — the shared key is already pulled
    94	into `.env.shared` by `npm run env -- init` (see `.env.sample`). Don't let the developer move on
    95	with this unresolved.
    96	
    97	Once all checks pass, say: "Setup is confirmed. Let's cover the rules and tools."
    98	
    99	---
   100	
   101	## Phase 3 — Developer orientation
   102	
   103	*Skip this phase for QA — go to Phase 4.*
   104	
   105	### Rules overview
   106	
   107	Walk through these in order — brief, one at a time, confirm understanding before continuing.
   108	
   109	**Branch rule (non-negotiable):**
   110	> "Never work directly on `develop` or `main`. Every task gets a feature branch.
   111	> Before each session: `git branch --show-current`. If it says develop, stop."
   112	
   113	**Protection tiers:**
   114	> "Every file in this repo has a tier. Tier 1 = frozen, you cannot touch it without explicit
   115	> owner approval. Tier 2 = protected, requires a second reviewer on the PR.
   116	> The Tier 1 list is in [.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md](../../rules/frozenFiles.md). Read it before your first task."
   117	
   118	Point them to the full tier map: [.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md](../../rules/frozenFiles.md) and [.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md](../../rules/protectedFiles.md).
   119	
   120	**TypeScript-only rule:**
   121	> "Every file you create or modify under `overrides/` must be `.ts` or `.tsx`.
   122	> `.js`/`.jsx` are not acceptable in that folder — including theme files, stories, and config modules.
   123	> Run `npx tsc --noEmit` before finishing any task that touches `overrides/`."
   124	
   125	**Hard Rule #12:**
   126	> "If requirements are unclear, Claude will ask one clarifying question at a time and wait.
   127	> If you're prompting Claude and it asks a question, answer it before sending the next instruction."
   128	
   129	**Contact map:**
   130	Read [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) contact map section. Tell them:
   131	> "Design tokens → UI Designer (#design-system). Commerce hooks → Integration Lead (#integration).
   132	> Checkout / cart → Squad A Lead. PDP / search / account → Squad B Lead."
   133	
   134	### Sprint order
   135	
   136	Read `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` and [.docs/memory/projectState.md](../../../.docs/memory/projectState.md). Tell them which sprint the project is currently in.
   137	
   138	> "We're in Sprint [N]. That means [what exists]. Code from Sprint [N+1] doesn't exist yet —
   139	> don't reference it in your tasks."
   140	
   141	### Squad-specific orientation
   142	
   143	**Squad A (checkout, cart, payments):**
   144	> "Your squad owns `overrides/app/pages/checkout/`, `overrides/app/components/order-summary/`,
   145	> `overrides/app/components/promo-code/`, and `overrides/app/components/pickup-or-delivery/`.
   146	> Before touching the header, footer, or shared product components, message Squad B Lead."
   147	
   148	**Squad B (PDP, PLP, search, account):**
   149	> "Your squad owns `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/`, `overrides/app/pages/product-list/`,
   150	> `overrides/app/pages/account/`, and `overrides/app/components/product-tile/`.
   151	> Before touching checkout or cart components, message Squad A Lead."
   152	
   153	### Key skills
   154	
   155	Tell them which skills to reach for first:
   156	- [/session-start](../session-start/SKILL.md) — run at the start of every session (mandatory)
   157	- [/feature-spec](../feature-spec/SKILL.md) — before starting any non-trivial implementation
   158	- [/code-quality](../code-quality/SKILL.md) — before opening a PR
   159	- [/pr-checklist](../pr-checklist/SKILL.md) — to generate PR description
   160	- [/qa-generate](../qa-generate/SKILL.md) — when you need E2E test coverage for a user journey
   161	
   162	### First task
   163	
   164	> "Your first task: read [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) and [.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md](../../rules/frozenFiles.md) end to end.
   165	> Then run `/session-start` to see the current project state.
   166	> When you have a ticket to work on, start with `/feature-spec` before writing any code."
   167	
   168	---
   169	
   170	## Phase 4 — QA orientation
   171	
   172	*Skip this phase for developers — they went through Phase 3.*
   173	
   174	### The QA model
   175	
   176	> "This project uses a human-in-the-lead QA model. Claude generates tests — you validate them.
   177	> A test is not complete until you have approved the Gherkin `.feature` file.
   178	> Never accept a Playwright spec without reading and confirming the `.feature` file first."
   179	
   180	### Testing layers
   181	
   182	Three layers, three purposes (per [AGENTS.md](../../../AGENTS.md) > Testing):
   183	1. **Vitest** — unit logic.
   184	2. **Storybook `play` functions** — component interactions.
   185	3. **Playwright** — E2E user journeys (this is where Gherkin lives).
   186	
   187	### Feature file workflow
   188	
   189	Walk through the workflow:
   190	1. Developer creates a Jira story.
   191	2. Developer runs [/qa-generate](../qa-generate/SKILL.md) in Claude Code.
   192	3. Claude drafts a Gherkin `.feature` file and **stops**.
   193	4. QA reads the `.feature` file — it's in `e2e/features/{area}/`.
   194	5. QA annotates corrections in the file with `# QA ANNOTATION: [correction]`.
   195	6. Developer runs `/qa-generate` again with the annotation.
   196	7. Claude updates the feature file (confirm), then generates the Playwright spec.
   197	
   198	Point them to `e2e/features/README.md` and the [Guide 4: E2E Testing — Playwright & Gherkin Repo Conventions](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/305528833) Confluence page.
   199	
   200	### Tags they must verify
   201	
   202	Every `.feature` file needs:
   203	- `@{JIRA-KEY}` — Jira traceability for Zephyr. **If missing, results won't sync.**
   204	- `@{area}` — functional area tag
   205	- `@p0` — only on confirmed critical paths (checkout, ATC, auth, PDP variant selection)
   206	
   207	> "If a feature file is missing the Jira tag, flag it to the developer before the test is generated."
   208	
   209	### Magento baseline regression
   210	
   211	> "Files in `e2e/features/regression/` document Magento 2 expected behaviour.
   212	> When a baseline test fails against SFCC, do NOT update it to pass.
   213	> Add `# DELTA:` and bring it to the next standup for classification."
   214	
   215	### BrowserStack and Zephyr
   216	
   217	> "BrowserStack cross-browser runs trigger automatically on PRs to `release/**`.
   218	> Results link to your Zephyr stories via BrowserStack Test Observability.
   219	> Check with the delivery lead that your Jira account has access to the BrowserStack project."
   220	
   221	### First task
   222	
   223	> "Your first task: read the [Guide 4: E2E Testing — Playwright & Gherkin Repo Conventions](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/305528833) Confluence page end to end.
   224	> Then review the reference `.feature` file under `e2e/features/checkout/`. If you spot anything that reads like a technical implementation detail rather than plain English, that's exactly the kind of thing to flag in an annotation."
   225	
   226	---
   227	
   228	## Phase 5 — Confirm and close
   229	
   230	Ask:
   231	> "Any questions before you start?"
   232	
   233	Answer questions, one at a time. Then close with:
   234	> "You're set up. Run `/session-start` at the start of every session — it reads the tracking
   235	> docs and confirms where the project is before any code is written.
   236	> If something is unclear mid-task, ask in #dev-team before running Claude Code on it."

=== prd/index.md ===
     1	# PRD Index (Confirmed Scope Only)
     2	
     3	*Last updated: 2026-06-25. Source of truth: Zimmermann Functional Requirements.xlsx (signed-off requirements).*
     4	
     5	This index defines which Product Requirement Documents (PRDs) are **authoritative and safe to implement** for the Zimmermann SFCC PWA frontend.
     6	
     7	Anything not listed under "Confirmed" is either out of scope or not yet documented — do not infer or implement.
     8	
     9	---
    10	
    11	## ✅ CONFIRMED & SAFE TO IMPLEMENT
    12	
    13	The following PRDs are based on confirmed, signed-off requirements. Agents may implement ONLY what is explicitly specified in these PRDs.
    14	
    15	- **regional.md**
    16	  Storefronts, URL prefixes, entry routing, mismatch detection, checkout ownership, currency/tax, Didomi consent defaults, marketing opt-in, GDPR (REG-001..067). Data migration, URL strategy, SEO and GEO have moved to **dataMigrationSeo.md**.
    17	
    18	- **dataMigrationSeo.md**

Include a summary of any must-fix issues at the top of the PR description. If must-fix issues are found, state them prominently and recommend resolving before opening the PR.
