=== commit-msg hook ===
     1	#!/bin/bash
     2	# commit-msg: enforces conventional commits format on every commit.
     3	#
     4	# Install: cp scripts/hooks/commit-msg .git/hooks/commit-msg
     5	#          chmod +x .git/hooks/commit-msg
     6	
     7	commit_msg=$(cat "$1")
     8	
     9	# Pass through merge commits, reverts, fixups, and WIP
    10	if echo "$commit_msg" | grep -qE '^(Merge|Revert|fixup!|squash!|WIP)'; then
    11	  exit 0
    12	fi
    13	
    14	# Conventional commits pattern
    15	# type(optional-scope): description
    16	# upstream-sync is a Zimmermann-specific type for PWA Kit sync changes
    17	pattern='^(feat|fix|docs|style|refactor|perf|test|build|ci|chore|upstream-sync)(\([a-z0-9/._-]+\))?: .{1,100}$'
    18	
    19	if ! echo "$commit_msg" | grep -qE "$pattern"; then
    20	  echo ""
    21	  echo "  ❌  Commit rejected — message does not follow conventional commits format."
    22	  echo ""
    23	  echo "  Required:  type(scope): short description"
    24	  echo ""
    25	  echo "  Types:"
    26	  echo "    feat           new feature"
    27	  echo "    fix            bug fix"
    28	  echo "    docs           documentation only"
    29	  echo "    style          formatting, no logic change"
    30	  echo "    refactor       neither fix nor feat"
    31	  echo "    perf           performance improvement"
    32	  echo "    test           adding or updating tests"
    33	  echo "    build          build system or dependency changes"
    34	  echo "    ci             CI/CD configuration"
    35	  echo "    chore          maintenance tasks"
    36	  echo "    upstream-sync  upstream Salesforce PWA Kit sync"
    37	  echo ""
    38	  echo "  Scope examples (optional but encouraged):"
    39	  echo "    product-tile  checkout  auth  header  search"
    40	  echo "    global-e  adyen  contentful  searchspring"
    41	  echo "    pwa-kit-runtime  commerce-sdk-react"
    42	  echo ""
    43	  echo "  Examples:"
    44	  echo "    feat(product-tile): add sale badge for discounted variants"
    45	  echo "    fix(checkout): resolve shipping method not persisting on refresh"
    46	  echo "    upstream-sync(pwa-kit-runtime): apply v3.18.0 SSR cache fix"
    47	  echo "    chore(deps): update @salesforce/commerce-sdk-react to 5.3.0"
    48	  echo "    test(use-current-basket): add guest basket merge coverage"
    49	  echo ""
    50	  exit 1
    51	fi
    52	
    53	exit 0

=== coderabbit.yaml 300-360 ===
300	    # ── PDP / PLP ────────────────────────────────────────────
301	    - path: "overrides/app/pages/product-detail/**"
302	      instructions: |
303	        SQUAD B — PDP. The product detail page is the primary conversion entry point.
304	
305	        Check for:
306	        - Variant selection logic — confirm all variation attributes still resolve correctly
307	        - Add to cart — confirm ATC still fires the Einstein sendAddToCart event
308	        - Image gallery — confirm mobile swipe and zoom still work after any changes
309	        - SSR data prefetch — confirm useProduct is still being prefetched server-side
310	        - Structured data — confirm schema.org Product markup is still present in the output
311	
312	    - path: "overrides/app/pages/product-list/**"
313	      instructions: |
314	        SQUAD B — PLP. Faceted search, refinements, and sorting are SEO-critical.
315	
316	        Check for:
317	        - URL-based refinement state — confirm filters are reflected in the URL for SEO
318	        - Pagination — confirm URL-based pagination is intact (not scroll-based pagination)
319	        - Refinement removal — confirm the "clear all" and individual remove buttons still work
320	        - Page Designer slot — confirm the promotional banner slot still renders
321	
322	    # ── QA feature files ─────────────────────────────────────
323	    - path: "e2e/features/**"
324	      instructions: |
325	        GHERKIN FEATURE FILES — source of truth for QA. Lead QA must validate before
326	        the paired Playwright spec is generated.
327	
328	        Check for:
329	        - Jira traceability tag present: @SFCC-NNN
330	        - Area tag present: @checkout, @search, @account, @pdp, @plp, or @integrations
331	        - P0 journeys tagged @p0 — verify the scenario qualifies (checkout, ATC, auth, PDP variant)
332	        - No technical implementation detail in scenario steps — no selectors, URLs, or code references
333	        - At least one happy path and one failure/edge scenario per feature file
334	        - Background block used for shared preconditions, not repeated in each scenario
335	        - File under 150 lines — flag if exceeded, suggest splitting by scenario group
336	        - Baseline regression files (in regression/) are prefixed BASELINE- and use
337	          @baseline @regression tags (no Jira key tag)
338	        - DELTA comments present where SFCC behaviour is known to differ from Magento baseline
339	
340	    # ── General hooks ────────────────────────────────────────
341	    - path: "overrides/app/hooks/**"
342	      instructions: |
343	        HOOKS — Shared application logic. Check every hook change for:
344	
345	        - Whether the return value shape has changed — even adding a key can cause
346	          consumer components to render differently if they spread the return value
347	        - Whether the hook adds a new required parameter — this is always a breaking change
348	        - Whether cleanup functions (useEffect return) are still present where needed
349	        - Whether the hook is safe to call during SSR (no window/document access without guards)
350	        - Whether React Query cache invalidation is correct after mutations
351

353	  # TOOLS — static analysis CodeRabbit runs automatically
354	  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
355	  tools:

=== releaseBranchesRules head ===
1	# Release & Hotfix Branch Rules
2	
3	**Read this file in full before taking any action when `git branch --show-current` matches `release/*` or `hotfix/*`.** These rules apply *in addition to* the Hard Rules in [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md). On `feature/*` and `fix/*` branches they do not apply and this file can be ignored.
4	
5	See the branch table in [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md) > Branch Rules for which branch merges where.
6	
7	## Back-merge rules (GitFlow)
8	
9	To prevent `develop` drifting from production:
10	- When a `release/*` branch is merged to `main` at go-live, it must also be merged back to `develop`.
11	- When a `hotfix/*` is merged to `main`, it must also be merged back to `develop`.
12	- When a `fix/release-*` is merged into its `release/*` parent and the release later ships, the forward-merge to `develop` happens as part of the release back-merge above — no separate action.
13	
14	## Release Branch Behaviour
15	
16	When on a `release/*` branch, the following rules apply in addition to all Hard Rules.
17	
18	**Before writing any code, always:**
19	1. State a plan — which files will change, what will change in each, and why.
20	2. Assess blast radius — how many components, hooks, or pages consume each file being changed? Flag explicitly if any file has more than 3 consumers or is Tier 2 or above.
21	3. Wait for explicit developer confirmation before making any edit, including trivial ones.
22	
23	**Allowed on release branches:**
24	- Read-only skills: `/generate-changelog`, `/pr-checklist`, `/code-quality`
25	- Trivial non-code changes (copy corrections, version bumps, feature flag toggles) — plan + confirm required
26	- Code logic fixes — only on a `fix/release-{version}_{description}` sub-branch, never directly on the release branch
27	
28	**Not allowed on release branches:**
29	- New features or scope additions not in the release
30	- Refactoring
31	- Dependency changes
32	- Tier 1 or Tier 2 file changes without the same owner approval required on feature branches
33	
34	**How to make a code fix on a release branch:**
35	
36	The fix PR targets the release branch. Once the release ships, the fix flows into `develop` via the release back-merge — do not open a separate PR from `fix/release-*` to `develop`.
37	
38	```bash
39	# Branch from the release branch — not from develop
40	git checkout release/v0.1.0
41	git checkout -b fix/release-v0.1.0-payment-error-description
42	
43	# Make the fix, open a PR targeting the release branch
44	gh pr create --base release/v0.1.0 --title "fix(checkout): SFCC-999 payment error on release"
45	```
46	The SIT gate will run against the PR before it can merge (when CI lands). See [architecture.md > Environments](architecture.md) for the full environment topology (Local · Dev · Test · SIT · UAT · Stage · Prod).

89	## Environments
90	
91	Six-tier topology spans **Local → Dev → SIT → UAT → Stage → Prod**. Each tier (other than Local) has its own SFCC realm, Contentful environment, and MuleSoft connections. Ownership splits across three zones — Digital, IT/NewStore, and Shared (Digital + Business).
92	
93	| #   | Tier            | Owner         | Purpose                                                                      | Third-party availability                                              | Deploy trigger                                                              |
94	| --- | --------------- | ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
95	| 1   | **Local**       | Digital       | Feature build on developer machines                                          | All services mocked (MSW stubs)                                       | `npm start`                                                                 |
96	| 2   | **Dev**         | Digital       | Integrated digital testing across all 6 storefronts, independent of NewStore | MuleSoft STG · NewStore Dev · Omneo STG · Narvar stub · Adyen sandbox | Merge to `develop`                                                          |
97	| 3   | **SIT**         | IT / NewStore | NewStore SIT and regression on its own cadence                               | NewStore STG · MuleSoft STG · Narvar STG · AP21 test                  | NewStore release cadence (parallel lane, non-blocking for Digital releases) |
98	| 4   | **UAT**         | Shared        | Business acceptance across all 6 regions                                     | NewStore STG · Narvar STG · Omneo STG · Adyen sandbox                 | Business approval gate                                                      |
99	| 5   | **Stage** (E2E) | Shared        | End-to-end testing with all third parties live; time-boxed booked windows    | NewStore STG · MuleSoft STG · Omneo STG · Narvar STG · Adyen sandbox  | Booked 2-week window                                                        |
100	| 6   | **Prod**        | Live          | Production; AU canary then flag-flip to remaining regions                    | NewStore PROD · MuleSoft PROD · Omneo PROD · Narvar PROD · Adyen PROD | Release manager + canary gate                                               |
101	
102	**Stage** is the contractual performance-test environment referenced under [Pre-Build Decisions #3](#3--performance-budgets-) — it mirrors production infrastructure (same MRT bundle class, CDN/edge configuration, SFCC realm tier).
103	
104	**QA workflow** ([`qa.yml`](../.github/workflows/qa.yml)) runs on every PR to `develop` and `release/**`: Vitest unit tests and Storybook interaction + `@storybook/addon-a11y` component-level accessibility checks (`storybook test --ci`), in parallel. Code-correctness checks that run before any environment is involved.
105	
106	**SIT gate** ([`digital-sit.yml`](../.github/workflows/digital-sit.yml)) runs on push/PR to `release/**`: Playwright `p0` specs, bundle-size check, MuleSoft contract tests, Lighthouse CI thresholds, LHCI trend gate. Environment-dependent checks against the deployed Dev tier. On merge to `develop` it also deploys to Dev. Production deploys are gated on a clean SIT gate run plus stakeholder approval through UAT and Stage.
107	
108	**MRT targets** in [mobify.config.js](../mobify.config.js) map one-to-one to the topology: `dev | sit | uat | stage | production`. `ENVIRONMENT_NAME` (`local | dev | sit | uat | stage | prod`) is the per-tier tag emitted to Sentry, New Relic, and GTM.
109	
110	## SSR Requirement (DMU-030)
111	
112	Server-side rendering is **mandatory** for product, category, and content pages (DMU-030, signed off). PWA Kit's SSR pipeline must be preserved — do not introduce client-only patterns (e.g. `typeof window !== 'undefined'` short-circuits, client-only data fetching on first paint, or `next/dynamic`-style `{ ssr: false }`) on these page types. Any componentry that cannot render on the server must be gated behind a hydration-safe boundary that still emits SEO-relevant markup on the server.
=== 142-160 Design Source of Truth ===
142	## Design Source of Truth
143	
144	Figma file "29 April 2026" is the **current working draft** — not a signed-off final design. Implementations based on it are client-preview builds and may need to be revised when designs are finalised. Do not treat any Figma-derived decision as confirmed without explicit sign-off.
145	
146	Desktop prototype at zimm-prototype.vercel.app is AI-generated and desktop-only — also not a signed-off final design.
147	
148	## Header Layout (based on draft Figma, subject to change)
149	
150	Two rows: top bar (nav + icons) and logo row. Implemented in `overrides/app/components/header/index.tsx`, with Chakra theme overrides split across `overrides/app/theme/components/header.ts` and `overrides/app/theme/components/listMenu.ts`.
151	
152	**Logo**: uses `BrandLogo` from the icons package (PWA default with the svg file replaced). The Z.IMMERSE variant has not been implemented yet.
153	
154	**ListMenu active-state gotcha**: `listMenuTriggerLinkActive` is JS-spread _after_ `listMenuTriggerLink` on the same `<Link>` element. Any `_after` key in the active style entirely replaces the base `_after` object — all CSS properties must be repeated, not just the overriding ones.
155	
156	**Icons deferred**: Boutique, Contact, Newsletter (HPC-015) — icon assets not provided yet.
157	
158	**Base functionality retained**: All hooks, the account popover, wishlist, store locator, and all existing props are unchanged. Only layout and visual style changed so far.
159	
160	## Contentful Content Type Management

148	
149	      # Extracts Jira issue keys (project key SFCC, per e2e/features/README.md's
150	      # @SFCC-NNN tag convention) referenced anywhere in the PR title, PR body,
151	      # or branch name — the same signal the GitHub-for-Jira app uses to link a
152	      # PR to an issue, so this needs no Jira API credentials of its own. Uses
153	      # `env:` rather than interpolating PR title/body directly into the run
154	      # script, since both are attacker-controllable text.
155	      # Consumed by e2e-browserstack: on a develop-targeted PR, BrowserStack
156	      # only runs when at least one key is found, scoped to that story's
157	      # Playwright tag(s). See testing.md > BrowserStack story scoping.
158	      - name: Detect Jira story keys
159	        id: jira
160	        env:
161	          PR_TITLE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}
162	          PR_BODY: ${{ github.event.pull_request.body }}
163	          BRANCH: ${{ github.head_ref }}
164	        run: |
165	          KEYS=$(printf '%s\n%s\n%s\n' "$PR_TITLE" "$PR_BODY" "$BRANCH" \
166	            | grep -oE 'SFCC-[0-9]+' | sort -u | tr '\n' ' ' | sed 's/ $//')
167	          echo "keys=$KEYS" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
168	
169	      # package.json/package-lock.json deliberately aren't in the e2e/vitest path
170	      # lists above: those two suites care about *runtime* behaviour, and most
171	      # lockfile churn (a devDependency bump, a transitive-dep resync) can't
172	      # affect what ships to the browser. Only a change to package.json's own
173	      # "dependencies" block (a real runtime dependency) should force them to
174	      # run. Storybook keeps the blanket file-level check above — it's cheap
175	      # enough that being conservative there doesn't matter.

=== weekly-agents.yml purpose ===
name: Weekly Agents

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 1 * * 1'   # Every Monday at 1am UTC (after upstream-release-watch at midnight)
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read
  issues: write
  pull-requests: read

jobs:
  quality-sweep:
    name: Quality sweep — missing tests or stories
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Find components and hooks without paired tests/stories
        id: sweep
        run: |
          missing=()

          # Components under overrides/app/components/ — TypeScript only per AGENTS.md.
          # Per Zimmermann convention every UI component must have a paired .stories.tsx;
          # a .test.ts(x) is required for logic-heavy components but not for every leaf.
          # Flag any component file that lacks BOTH a story and a test.
          while IFS= read -r file; do
            base="${file%.*}"
            dir=$(dirname "$file")
            name=$(basename "$base")
            found=false
            # Check for paired test or story (same basename or co-located in the same folder)
            for t in "${base}.test.ts" "${base}.test.tsx" "${base}.stories.tsx" \
                     "${dir}/${name}.test.ts" "${dir}/${name}.test.tsx" "${dir}/${name}.stories.tsx" \
                     "${dir}/index.test.ts" "${dir}/index.test.tsx" "${dir}/index.stories.tsx"; do
              [[ -f "$t" ]] && found=true && break
            done
            $found || missing+=("$file")
